question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, state institutions, and military, with recent personnel purges further consolidating his authority and eliminating potential rivals ahead of the 2027 National Congress. No successor has been publicly positioned, and analysts note the absence of visible internal divisions or challenges that could force an early exit before the end of 2026. Trader consensus at 95.5% for continued tenure reflects this structural dominance and precedent of extended rule. Unlikely but plausible shifts could still arise from sudden health developments, elite realignments, or major external crises disrupting stability.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains highly fragmented more than two years before the primaries, with Gavin Newsom holding a modest lead in trader consensus due to his California governorship, national fundraising network, and visibility on issues like climate and immigration. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Jon Ossoff follow closely, reflecting progressive base strength and Senate battleground appeal, while Kamala Harris's position shows lingering name recognition tempered by 2024 results. This tight spread stems from the absence of an early frontrunner, ongoing party rebuilding after the prior cycle, and anticipation of 2026 midterm outcomes that could elevate or sideline candidates through new polling data, endorsements, and primary positioning. Future catalysts such as Senate confirmation fights, state-level policy wins, or debate performances could quickly consolidate support ahead of the Iowa caucuses and Super Tuesday.
